proposal.reactor_type: tubular PFA coil reactor (single integrated stage)
proposal.residence_time_basis: total combined reactor volume divided by total volumetric flow rate of all liquid streams at operating temperature
proposal.light_setup: none – thermal oxidation/amidation, no photochemistry required

streams.contents: benzyl alcohol (1.0 equiv) + morpholine (1.0 equiv) + NaBr (0.10 equiv)
streams.notes: NaBr dissolved directly; concentration is 2× target so that 1:1 mixing with S2 gives 0.667 M in reactor

streams.contents: TBHP (3.0 equiv, 70 wt% aqueous solution diluted in dioxane) + H2SO4 (0.20 equiv)
streams.solvent: 1,4-dioxane (with residual water from TBHP aqueous solution, ~5 vol%)
streams.molar_equiv: TBHP 3.0 relative to benzyl alcohol, H2SO4 0.20
streams.notes: TBHP excess (3 equiv) ensures complete oxidation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde intermediate and subsequent amidation; H2SO4 activates NaBr in situ to generate HBr/Br2 oxidant shuttle

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PEEK, 0.5 mm bore) followed by 10 cm static mixing zone in PFA tubing before reactor coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: S1 (substrate + amine + NaBr) and S2 (TBHP + acid) are kept separate until the T-mixer immediately upstream of the heated reactor coil. Premixing TBHP with acid and NaBr risks premature Br2 generation and substrate oxidation at room temperature. Introducing the amine in S1 rather than S2 prevents acid-induced protonation of morpholine before mixing, which would deactivate it. The T-mixer provides rapid micromixing (estimated mixing time < 1 s at 0.4 mL/min in 1 mm ID) before the reaction zone.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare S1: dissolve benzyl alcohol (1.334 M), morpholine (1.334 M), and NaBr (0.1334 M) in dry 1,4-dioxane; degas with N2 sparging for 10 min
Prepare S2: dilute 70 wt% aqueous TBHP to 2.001 M in 1,4-dioxane; add H2SO4 (0.267 M); degas with N2 sparging for 10 min
Prime both pump lines and purge dead volume (≥ 3 reactor volumes) before collecting product
Set BPR to 6.9 bar and verify back-pressure stability before heating reactor coil
Heat reactor coil to 100 °C and confirm temperature stability (±1 °C) before starting collection
post_reactor_steps: Effluent passes through BPR (6.9 bar) to maintain liquid phase and suppress TBHP decomposition gas evolution inside reactor
Collect effluent into aqueous Na2SO3 quench solution (10 wt%, 2 vol equiv) to destroy residual TBHP
Basify with sat. NaHCO3 to pH 8–9 to neutralize H2SO4 and protonate morpholinium
Extract with EtOAc (3×), dry over MgSO4, filter, concentrate under reduced pressure
Optional: column chromatography (SiO2, hexane/EtOAc 3:1) if purity < 95% by 1H NMR
proposal.chemistry_notes: The reaction proceeds via a two-step tandem sequence in a single reactor zone: (1) NaBr/H2SO4/TBHP oxidizes benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde via a bromine-mediated radical/ionic mechanism; (2) the in-situ-generated benzaldehyde undergoes oxidative amidation with morpholine using excess TBHP to give benzoylmorpholine. Both steps are thermally driven; no photocatalysis is required. The elevated temperature (100 °C vs. 80 °C batch) compensates for the shorter residence time (15 min vs. 30 min) and the reduced mixing efficiency relative to a stirred batch vessel. The BPR at 6.9 bar keeps dioxane (bp 101 °C) and water fully liquid at 100 °C and suppresses TBHP decomposition to tert-butanol + O2 (which would create gas slugs). PFA tubing is chosen for chemical resistance to TBHP, H2SO4, and HBr. Dioxane is retained as solvent to match batch conditions; a switch to DMF or NMP could improve solubility but would complicate workup.

stage_1_oxidation_and_amidation.description: Combined oxidation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde and oxidative amidation with morpholine
stage_1_oxidation_and_amidation.key_reagents: TBHP (3.0 equiv), NaBr (0.10 equiv), H2SO4 (0.20 equiv)

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Batch required 30 min at 80 °C. Arrhenius scaling: assuming Ea ~80 kJ/mol (typical radical oxidation), a 20 °C increase (80→100 °C) gives rate factor exp[(80000/8.314)×(1/353 – 1/373)] ≈ 2.1×. Therefore 30/2.1 ≈ 14.3 min; rounded up to 15 min to provide safety margin and account for flow non-idealities.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Two pumps each at 0.2 mL/min → total 0.4 mL/min. Chosen to give reactor volume = 0.4 × 15 = 6.0 mL, a practical coil size. Lower flow rates risk thermal decomposition of TBHP; higher rates require larger reactor.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 100 °C selected to accelerate kinetics vs. 80 °C batch while remaining below dioxane bp (101 °C) at ambient pressure; BPR maintains liquid phase.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.667 M in reactor matches batch concentration exactly, achieved by preparing each stream at 1.334 M and mixing 1:1.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 6.9 bar (≈100 psi) chosen to keep dioxane/water mixture liquid at 100 °C (dioxane bp 101 °C at 1 bar; at 6.9 bar bp > 140 °C) and to suppress O2 evolution from TBHP decomposition. Standard BPR setting for dioxane at 100 °C in flow chemistry.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Tubular PFA coil is standard for oxidative flow chemistry; provides plug flow, good heat transfer, and chemical resistance.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA: resistant to TBHP, H2SO4, HBr, dioxane. SS would corrode with HBr; PTFE acceptable but PFA more flexible for coiling.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID: balances pressure drop (manageable at 0.4 mL/min), mixing quality, and wall effects. Smaller ID (0.5 mm) would give excessive pressure drop over 6 mL volume.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: V = Q × t_r = 0.4 mL/min × 15 min = 6.0 mL. Coil length = V / (π × (0.5 mm)² ) = 6000 mm³ / 0.785 mm² ≈ 7640 mm ≈ 7.6 m of 1 mm ID tubing.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_safety: 6.9 bar is well within PFA tubing pressure rating (typically >20 bar at 100 °C for 1/16 inch OD PFA). TBHP decomposition pressure contribution is suppressed by BPR.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_inlet_min: 15.0 min based on nominal flow rate and reactor volume at inlet conditions.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_in_channel_min: Corrected for thermal expansion of dioxane at 100 °C (density ~0.97 g/mL vs. 1.03 g/mL at 20 °C, ~6% volume expansion): 15.0 / 1.06 ≈ 14.2 min. Assumption: linear thermal expansion correction applied to liquid density.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemistry; reaction is purely thermal.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer provides rapid impingement mixing. PEEK material resists acid and TBHP. 0.5 mm bore gives Re > 100 at 0.4 mL/min in dioxane, ensuring turbulent-like mixing at junction.

literature_analogies: Bogdan, A. R.; Sach, N. W. Adv. Synth. Catal. 2009, 351, 849–854: TBHP-mediated oxidative amidation of alcohols in flow using PFA tubing at elevated temperature and BPR.
Petersen, T. P. et al. Chem. Eur. J. 2015, 21, 10, 3994: NaBr/TBHP oxidation of benzyl alcohols to aldehydes in continuous flow.
Gutmann, B. et al. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2015, 54, 7219: General review of oxidative flow chemistry with peroxides, emphasizing BPR necessity above solvent bp.
Deadman, B. J. et al. Chem. Commun. 2013, 49, 4521: Tandem oxidation–amidation in flow; residence time scaling from batch via Arrhenius correction.
Assumption: Ea = 80 kJ/mol is an estimate for NaBr/TBHP alcohol oxidation; actual value not found in literature for this exact system. Temperature correction should be validated experimentally.
safety_flags: TBHP (70 wt% aqueous): organic peroxide, flammable, oxidizer – store cold, avoid contact with metals, reducing agents, and strong acids until point of mixing; use secondary containment
H2SO4: corrosive – handle with PPE; neutralize waste before disposal
NaBr + H2SO4 + TBHP generate HBr and Br2 in situ: toxic, corrosive vapors – ensure reactor is fully enclosed and effluent is vented to scrubber (10% NaOH solution)
1,4-Dioxane: flammable (flash point 12 °C), suspected carcinogen – use in fume hood; avoid peroxide formation in stored solvent (test with peroxide strips before use)
Reactor at 100 °C above dioxane bp: BPR failure could cause flash vaporization – install pressure relief valve rated at 10 bar upstream of BPR; use blast shield
TBHP decomposition produces O2 and tert-butanol: O2 enrichment in enclosed reactor could create flammable atmosphere with dioxane vapor – ensure BPR is functioning before heating
Quench with Na2SO3 solution immediately at reactor outlet to destroy residual TBHP before open-vessel workup
All connections should be rated for at least 15 bar at 120 °C; inspect PFA tubing for discoloration or swelling before each run
Emergency: have water spray and dry chemical extinguisher available; do not use CO2 on peroxide fires

confidence.notes: Confidence limited by: (1) assumed Ea for Arrhenius scaling not experimentally verified for this specific NaBr/TBHP/H2SO4 system; (2) two-step tandem mechanism may have different rate-limiting steps in flow vs. batch; (3) dioxane near its bp at 100 °C introduces risk – consider switching to DMF (bp 153 °C) if BPR reliability is a concern; (4) NaBr solubility in dioxane at 1.334 M should be verified (NaBr is sparingly soluble in dioxane; may require co-solvent water or switch to NaBr aqueous solution added as third stream).
